chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْه، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام: مِنْ سَعَادَةِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينَ أَنِّي ذَكَرْتُهُ فِي الْمَوْقِفِ

translations.en: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: One of the felicities of Ali ibn Yaqtin is that I remembered him [supplicated for him] at the Mawqif.

en.summary: This hadith from Al-Kashi highlights the spiritual elevation of Ali ibn Yaqtin, a prominent companion, through the specific mention of his name by Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) during the Mawqif at Arafat. In Shia tradition, the Imam's remembrance of a follower during the pivotal moment of standing at Arafat signifies divine acceptance and a unique bond of intercession, underscoring the role of the Imam as the spiritual guide who elevates his followers' status before God.
en.seo_question: What is the significance of being remembered by the Imam at the Mawqif?

key_terms.مَوْقِف: the standing place, specifically referring to Arafat during Hajj
